thesis_summary.thesis: Gold Royalty Corp. (GROY) is a Vancouver-based precious metals royalty and streaming company listed on NYSE American and the TSX. **[Fact]** The company holds a portfolio of gold-focused royalties, streams, and land-agreement interests on mines operated by third parties across the Americas and other regions; it has no mine operating staff and reports in U.S. dollars under IFRS. **[Fact]** GROY was spun out of GoldMining Inc. in 2021 and follows a dual strategy: acquiring cash-flowing royalties and a lower-cost "royalty generator" land model that creates pre-production royalties from surface agreements. **[Fact]** FY2025 royalty revenue was a record $15.6 million (+55% year-over-year), total revenue including land proceeds and interest was $17.8 million, and operating cash flow was $6.2 million on 188.0 million weighted-average shares. **[Fact]** At December 31, 2025 the company had no outstanding debt, $12.4 million cash, and $75.0 million available on its secured revolving credit facility; 224.5 million common shares were outstanding.
thesis_summary.why_market_wrong: The stock may look like a low-yield micro-cap royalty stub while underpricing a growing producing base plus a large book of non-producing royalties. **[Inference]** FY2025 revenue was concentrated in four mines (Borborema, Côté Gold, Cozamin, Vares = 79.7% of revenue), but Borborema reached commercial production only in 2025 and Canadian Malartic's Odyssey underground project (38.6% of balance-sheet asset weight) is advancing on schedule. **[Inference]** Reported net loss of $4.1 million overstates economic weakness: adjusted EBITDA was a record $9.8 million and adjusted net loss was $1.7 million after stripping fair-value noise on the repaid gold-linked loan and other non-recurring items. **[Inference]** Royalty interests are carried at cost on the balance sheet, so book value (~$3.11 per share at year-end) does not mark portfolio metal exposure or development optionality at spot prices.
